description: The machine-checkable half of docs/__meta__/arch-prd.md#2-frontmatter and docs/__meta__/arch-prd.md#3-sections. No section has a word cap and the file has no token budget.

name.description: prd-<NNN>-<feature>: the document number docs/__meta__/arch.md allocates, one sequence shared by every document in docs/arch/, then the feature in a few kebab-case words. See docs/__meta__/arch-prd.md#1-naming.

status.description: approved once no open question is left; frozen once shipped or dropped.

outline.description: Who needs the feature, what they cannot do today, and why it matters now, in one or two paragraphs.
examples: An agent's shell command is a small program...

outline.description: The outcomes the feature commits to, as a bulleted list.
What a reader might expect the feature to do and it does not, each with the reason it is out of scope.

Prioritised user stories, each under an H3 that gives its identifier, title and priority, each with an independent test and one or more scenarios, each a gherkin block of its own holding one Scenario: and no Feature:.
examples:
### US-1: Parse shell commands (P1)

As an analyst, I want to parse shell command lines, so that I can inspect command shapes.

**Independent test:** Parse a single bash line.

```gherkin
Scenario: Parse pipeline
  Given a shell command
  When parsed
  Then commands are extracted
```

outline.description: Numbered FR- and NFR- items, one behaviour each, each in one EARS pattern; an unknown is marked [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …] inline.
examples:
- **FR-001:** THE SYSTEM SHALL report every finding with the path of the document it was found in.
- **NFR-001:** THE SYSTEM SHALL check a workspace in under two seconds.

outline.description: Boundary conditions and failure paths the user stories do not cover, as questions.
examples: - What happens when input is truncated?

outline.description: The concepts the requirements name, what each is to the user and how it relates to the others, without its representation.
Numbered SC- items, each a measurable outcome stated without naming the technology.
examples: - **SC-001:** Analysts can group command shapes by error status.

outline.description: What the requirements take for granted, as a bulleted list.
Every [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker in the document, gathered under the identifier of the requirement that carries it.
examples: - **FR-005:** In every output format, or in the text output only?

outline.description: The design documents and decision records it leads to, as Leads to. Never a feat doc: the feat doc links the PRD instead.
examples: - [adr-002](adr-002-shell-parser.md) - Leads to: How the parser is built
